title: WPMS/631/2014 of M/s Harbans Lal Sahni and Sons Vs Uttarakhand Krishi Utpadan Vipanan Board AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 631 of 2014
M/s Harbans Lal Shahni and sons through its
proprietor Smt. Kavita Sahni .....Petitioner
Versus
Uttarakhand Krishi Utpadan
Vipanan Board and Another ....Respondents
Advocate : Mr. Ajay Veer Pundir, Advocate for the petitioner.
 Mrs. Monika Pant, Advocate for the respondents.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
As per the facts of the case are that the petitioner has been
allotted a shop bearing Shop No. B-9, as back as in the year 2001. Later
on, in the year 2008, he was allotted a Godown by an order dated 31st
January 2008, being Godown No. 9 and as per the terms of the allotment,
it is the case of the petitioner that he was levied with the rent payable on
the godown thus allotted @ Rs. 1530/- per month and accordingly, he
continued to remit the rent at the said rate consistently without there
being any default committed by him.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner
is aggrieved by a communication which has been issued to him by
respondent No. 2 on 8th February 2012, whereby the respondent had
resorted to the process of imposing the rate of rent @ Rs. 3333/- as well
as also claiming for the arrears of the rent from the date of allotment till
the date of the issuance of the impugned order dated 8th February 2012.
Being aggrieved against the said order of imposing the enhanced rent of
Rs. 3333/- per month, the petitioner had preferred an appeal before the
respondent being Appeal No. 24 of 2014, M/s Harbans Lal Shahni and
sons v. Krishi Utpadan Mandi Samiti, Roorkee (Haridwar).
3. In the appeal in question, which was preferred against
enhanced imposition of rent, when the petitioner has contesting the

2
matter one fact, it was then it has been revealed to him is that admittedly
the rent which was levied on him for the Godown allotted at the rate of
Rs. 1530/- per month on 31st August 2008, in fact, it was by virtue of a
clerical mistake, though, in fact, admittedly for the godowns of the like
nature, the rate of rent actually settled was of Rs. 3333/- payable by the
occupants of the Godowns, to whom it was allotted. It was by there
mistake that petitioner was levied with lesser rent @ Rs. 1530/- p.m.
which has been rectified by the impugned action.
4. This writ petition was listed on 7th October 2017 and the
same was dismissed for want of prosecution. The petitioner has preferred
a Restoration Application No. 334/2019 along with the Delay
Condonation Application 5590/2019, seeking condonation of delay of
536 days, which have chanced in filing the Restoration Application.
Having considered the reasons, assigned in the delay condonation
application and also after hearing the counsel for the respondent on the
said issue, since the delay is not being seriously opposed, the Delay
Condonation Application is allowed and the delay of 536 days which has
chanced in preferring the Restoration Application would stand condoned.
5. Also heard the learned counsel for the parties on the
Restoration Application and the reasons, which has been assigned in the
Restoration Application for absence on that date is to the effect that the
office of the counsel was unable to mark the cause list due to which he
could not put in appearance on the date fixed in the matter. The reasons
as expressed in the Restoration Application is satisfactory on account of
the fact that basic spirit of dispensation of justice is that no litigants
should suffer on account of the mistake committed by the counsel or
his/her office in marking the cause list, Consequently, the Restoration
Application too would stand allowed and the writ petition is restored to
its original number.

3
6. The parties with consent are heard on merits. In the writ
petition, the petitioner has not come up with case, as orally argued today
by the counsel for the petitioner that the location of the Godown which
was allotted to her is of such a nature which according to the norms
settled by the Mandi Samiti would be fetching, are lesser no such norms
are pleaded or produced by the petitioner. This is not the case, which has
been pleaded in the writ petition nor there is any material in that regard
that the rates of rent which has been fixed by the Mandi Samiti varies
with the location of the godown. Hence this argument of the learned
counsel for the petitioner is not acceptable by this court being beyond the
scope of writ petition.
7. The Other aspect of the matter is that when the writ petition
was dismissed for want of prosecution and even prior to it, after the
dismissal of the writ petition, the petitioner herself has written a letter to
the Secretary, Mandi Samiti on 22nd April 2019, wherein she has
expressed her willingness to remit the entire arrears of the rent of the said
Godown which has been sought to be recovered by the impugned order
dated 8th February 2012. In view of the said undertaking given on 22nd
April 2019 and also considering the fact that the lesser rent was imposed
on the petitioner on account of the clerical mistakes, the fact which is not
denied by the petitioner in the writ petition, this Court finds that a
rectification of the clerical mistake by a subsequent order dated 8th
February 2012, cannot be said to be arbitrary, because in fact, rather it
was a revival of the actual liability which otherwise the petitioner was
entitled to cater as a consequence of the allotment of the Godown made
in her favour like the other allottees and the petitioner cannot be meted
out with a different treatment.
8. Consequently, this Court is of the view that looking to the
reasons which has been assigned in the Appellate Order and also
considering the undertaking already given by the petitioner, the petitioner
cannot be meted out with the different treatment as compared to the other

4
allottees, who were identically placed, to whom the Godowns have been
allotted on the same rate of rent i.e. of Rs. 3333/- per month.
Consequently, this Court does not find any merits in the writ petition and
the same is accordingly dismissed. However, there would be no order as
to cost.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 31.05.2019
Mahinder/
